catalogue_title: Antidiagonal local curves and integral exponents in universal curve counting
title: Antidiagonal local curves and integral exponents in universal curve counting
label: Universal curve counting

related.label: Companion paper on scalar product exponents

abstract_html: Assuming Pardon's Gromov–Witten evaluation for analytic families of threefolds, we lift the elementary-cluster expansion to his rational algebra of one-cycles. For each genus we construct a universal local factor from the circle action with opposite weights on the two summands of a balanced local Calabi–Yau curve. For every smooth projective Calabi–Yau threefold with torsion-free second homology, the universal curve-counting series is a unique product of these factors with integer exponents. The exponents are the elementary-cluster coefficients of Ionel and Parker. To construct the factors, we project a cycle onto the two line summands and use the resulting symmetric functions to isolate each multiple of the zero section. The associated compactly supported classes respect addition of cycles and multiplication by positive integers, and their Gromov–Witten evaluations are the local series of Bryan and Pandharipande. The corresponding stable-pair evaluation gives a second proof of exponent integrality.
